mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille sequence: notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public then New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Apostille certificate. Consular Legalization sequence for non-Hague states: notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public, then authenticated by the Department of Internal Affairs, then authenticated by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, then legalized by the destination-state consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille sequence: notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public then Department of Internal Affairs Apostille. Consular Legalization sequence for non-Hague states: notarised and then carried through Department of Internal Affairs and Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade authentications followed by consular legalization at the destination embassy. The two authentication paths are parallel and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation and regulatory filing actions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed shareholders and directors of New Zealand Limited, executed before a New Zealand Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: notarisation followed by Department of Internal Affairs Apostille. Non-Hague path: notarisation followed by Department of Internal Affairs authentication, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade authentication, and final consular legalization by the destination state. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative mechanisms, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company shareholders and incorporator, certified by a New Zealand solicitor/Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille sequence: certified copy notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public then apostilled by the Department of Internal Affairs. Consular Legalization sequence for non-member states: certified copy notarised, authenticated by the Department of Internal Affairs, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, then consularised by the destination-state embassy. The two paths are exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the company's existing or intended bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorised bank officer at a New Zealand registered bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille sequence: bank officer signature notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public then Apostille issued by the Department of Internal Affairs. Consular Legalization sequence: bank officer signature notarised, Department of Internal Affairs authentication, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade authentication, and destination consulate legalization. No chaining of Apostille with consular legalization is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every beneficial owner, director, proposed shareholder, and authorised signatory must be screened in real time against the New Zealand Police designated terrorist list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the United Kingdom and European Union sanctions lists, the Australian DFAT consolidated list, and all New Zealand sanctions lists maintained under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and the United Nations Act 1946. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, and for clients connected to high-risk jurisdictions or negative media. The 25% ownership threshold triggers statutory UBO identification and verification. Source of funds and source of wealth must be documented in writing for every high-risk engagement or jurisdiction. All screening results, risk rationales, and customer due diligence files must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online company name availability and registration portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English or Maori; Maori diacritical marks are permitted but are treated as equivalent to unmarked letters for deceptively-similar checks. Non-Latin script names must be phonetically transliterated into the Latin alphabet in the Companies Office record. The four-tier naming convention is applied as follows: exact name match is automatically refused; homophonic or visually deceptively similar names are refused; hyphenated, compound, or combined equivalents are compared as one continuous string; and foreign-language translated equivalents of existing New Zealand company names are treated as confusingly similar and refused unless written consent is lodged.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant must file a written appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 15 working days from the date of the rejection notice. The appeal must identify the rejected name, cite the relevant Companies Act 1993 name restriction, attach the Companies Office rejection notice, and include legal submissions plus registry search results showing that the name is not identical or deceptively similar. If the name contains a sensitive token, a formal consent letter from the relevant Minister or regulator must be attached. The Registrar must then make a fresh decision; if the appeal is again declined, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for review under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 or re-file a materially different name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For this MedTech FDA 510(k) filing and European CE Mark regulatory consultancy, a pure virtual commercial mailbox will generally be rejected by the Inland Revenue Department for GST registration and by New Zealand banks for corporate account opening if there is no verifiable physical place of operation. A virtual address may be used for service of process only if the registered office is maintained by a chartered accountant or licensed corporate agent at a physical New Zealand street address, and the company must retain its registers, AML/CFT files, client contracts, and accounting records at an accessible physical location. Banks and IRD may classify a letterbox-only company as shell-like and demand proof of actual staff, local management, and operational substance before approving banking or tax arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist includes: physical registered-office sign or reception; access to company registers and statutory records; original board and shareholder resolutions; AML/CFT customer due diligence and UBO files; accounting and GST tax records; client engagement contracts for FDA/CE consulting; lease or home-office evidence; utility invoices; bank statements; and employment or contractor records. Quantified risk: low-to-moderate for a newly incorporated low-risk medical device regulatory consultancy, estimated at 20% annual probability of an unannounced inspection by the Companies Office or IRD; probability increases to approximately 45% if the company claims GST refunds, uses a virtual office, or has no verifiable operational address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), sections 10 to 16 (incorporation procedure and certificate of incorporation), section 26 (registered office), sections 60 to 70 (constitution), sections 151 to 153 (appointment and residency requirements of directors), section 52 (share capital account), and Schedule 2 (default constitution rules); complemented by the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for financial statement preparation and audit exemption thresholds.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), acting through the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Company (Form NZCN006) filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: New Zealand imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 1993. Shares are issued without par value and may be paid in full, in part, or on deferred terms as determined by the board. No escrow account, capital deposit, or capital verification certificate is required at incorporation. An applicant need only state the proposed shareholding structure and consideration terms in the Application for Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the first meeting of the board of directors of [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the Company) is lawfully constituted and the following resolutions are duly passed: 1. Constitution. The Constitution presented to this meeting, in the form attached to the Application for Incorporation, is adopted as the Company's Constitution, binding the Company and every shareholder under the Companies Act 1993. 2. Share Capital. The issue and allotment of [NUMBER] ordinary shares, without nominal value, at an issue price of NZD [AMOUNT] per share, to the subscribers named in the Application for Incorporation, is ratified. Payment of consideration is accepted and credited to the Company's share capital account in accordance with section 52 of the Companies Act 1993. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is established at [STREET ADDRESS], [CITY], New Zealand, and the Registrar of Companies shall be notified of any change. 4. Directors. [NAME 1] and [NAME 2] are appointed as the first directors, each having executed a written consent to act under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993. 5. Bank Mandate. The directors are authorised to open and maintain corporate bank accounts with [BANK], to appoint signatories, and to govern banking mandates. All resolutions were carried unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online portal (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a live name search on the New Zealand Companies Register at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz. Verify the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, does not imply Crown affiliation or a restricted activity (e.g., banking, insurance, trust, university) without written consent from the responsible Ministry, and complies with section 21 of the Companies Act 1993. The suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' is mandatory for a limited liability company. If the desired name is available, it may be used immediately in the incorporation application; a formal reservation is not compulsory but is recommended to secure the name for up to 20 working days before filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (with mandatory 'Limited' or 'Ltd' suffix)
Certified extract of the Companies Register name search results
List of any restricted words requiring regulatory consent, together with the relevant consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried by the Registrar under section 21, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the New Zealand Companies Office within 15 working days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or regulatory consent; alternatively, the applicant may amend the name and resubmit the incorporation application at no additional statutory disadvantage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution, Share Structure, and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company promoters and external legal counsel (no government filing required at this stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution or elect to rely on the default rules in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993. Determine the authorised share structure (one class of ordinary shares is standard), the number of directors (minimum one), and the proposed shareholders. Confirm statutory compliance such that at least one director resides in New Zealand or Australia as required by section 153(1) of the Companies Act 1993. Obtain each proposed director's written consent to act in the prescribed form, ensure no person is disqualified from holding office, and compile proof of identity and residential address for AML/CFT onboarding. Establish the physical New Zealand registered office address (a post office box is not acceptable under section 189(3)).
required_dossiers: Constitution (or confirmation of reliance on Schedule 2 default rules)
Shareholders' agreement (if any) and proposed share allotment schedule
Directors' consent to act forms (prescribed consent form)
Certified copies of directors' passports and proof of residential address
Statement confirming at least one director satisfies the New Zealand/Australian residency requirement
Registered office address and address for service in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: All deficiencies are curable at the drafting stage before filing. If the Registrar subsequently questions the validity of a director's consent or residency, the company may file a replacement consent form or appoint a compliant director by supplementary board resolution and notify the Registrar under section 153 within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Application for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies - New Zealand Companies Office electronic registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form NZCN006 (Application for Incorporation of a Company) electronically through the Companies Register. Enter the approved company name, the registered office address, the address for service, the full names and residential addresses of all directors and shareholders, the share structure, and attach the constitution if adopted. Confirm each director's written consent is held and certify that all directors meet eligibility requirements under sections 151 and 152 of the Companies Act 1993. Pay the statutory fee of NZD 105.00 by credit card or bank transfer. Submit the application electronically; the Registrar reviews for completeness and compliance prior to issuing the certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NZCN006 (online)
Company constitution (if not relying on default rules)
Directors' consents to act (retained by the company; not filed unless requested)
Proof of registered office address
Payment of official filing fee (NZD 105.00)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, the applicant must respond within 10 working days through the Companies Register online portal with corrected or supplementary information. If the application is refused, the applicant may re-file a corrected application with payment of a new fee, or seek statutory review of the Registrar's decision before the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies / New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE), administered via the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation under section 14 of the Companies Act 1993, and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is automatically allocated. The company is constituted as a separate legal entity as of the date on the certificate. Download and store the certificate and the NZBN registration record. Verify the legal name, entity type (Limited Company), registered office, and directors' details on the public Companies Register; correct any typographical or administrative errors promptly.
required_dossiers: Application reference number from Step 3
Payment receipt confirming filing fee
Email confirmation of registration from the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or registered particulars contain errors, file an application for administrative correction with the Registrar under section 15(2) of the Companies Act 1993, supplying documentary evidence of the correct details. If the certificate is lost, obtain a certified copy from the Companies Register at a nominal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Inland Revenue (IRD Number, GST, PAYE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD) - myIR online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with Inland Revenue to obtain an IRD number using the online myIR registration or paper form IR596. State the business activity as 'medical device regulatory consulting services' (ISIC 7490). Register for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; GST registration is compulsory where annual taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000, and voluntary registration is typically advisable for business-to-business consultancy to recover input credits. If staff will be hired, register as a PAYE employer. Confirm the Entity_Level_Taxation status: company income is taxed at the corporate rate of 28% under the Income Tax Act 2007, with provisional tax obligations for anticipated residual income tax above NZD 5,000.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN number
Director identification documents (IRD and company director number)
Bank account details for refunds and payments
Estimated turnover and commencement date of business
Declaration of business activity classification (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541690 equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is queried or delayed beyond the service standard, the applicant may log into myIR, review the exchange message, and resubmit missing information. For unresolved delays, escalate via the IRD Business Tax contact centre or contact the IRD agent services team; no penalty applies while the Registrations are in progress provided the entity acts promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Compliance and Corporate Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company internal governance (board) and commercial banks supervised by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand under the AML/CFT Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro forma first board resolution (share capital ratification, registered office adoption, director appointments, and bank mandate). Establish statutory records: the share register, the register of directors, the register of charges, and the company constitution, each maintained at the registered office in accordance with sections 89 to 95 of the Companies Act 1993. Display the company name at the registered office. File an annual return within the prescribed period (no fee) and, if required by the Financial Reporting Act 2013, prepare and file financial statements with the Companies Office. Open a corporate bank account with an approved New Zealand bank; banks will require certified incorporation documents, a beneficial ownership declaration, and FATCA/CRS self-certification of the underlying shareholders.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Company constitution and first board resolution
Directors' certified passports and proof of residential address
Beneficial ownership declaration (identifying all individuals with 25% or more control)
FATCA/CRS self-certification forms for shareholders
Bank account application and signatory mandate resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines or conditionally approves the application under AML/CFT requirements, the applicant should provide supplemental KYC evidence (e.g., certified corporate registry extract, trust deed if a foreign trust holds shares, reference letter from the applicant's home-country bank). Alternatively, approach another registered New Zealand bank or non-bank deposit taker, or request a formal review of the adverse decision through the bank's internal AML/CFT compliance officer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. No industrial operating licence is required for ISIC 7490 medical device regulatory consulting. For reference, New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority (Medsafe), operating under the Ministry of Health, is the competent authority for medical device regulation under the Medicines Act 1981 and the Therapeutic Products Act 2023 framework; however, a consultancy that provides FDA 510(k) and CE mark filing services to clients does not itself manufacture, distribute, or supply medical devices and therefore requires no Medsafe licence or conformity assessment approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No operational permit or manufacturing licence. The scope of the entity is confined to professional advisory services in medical device regulatory strategy, application compilation, and European CE marking consultation, which is unlicensed in New Zealand. No Medicines Act 1981 license, No Food Act 2014 registration, and no Hazardous Substances and New Organisms (HSNO) Act 1996 approval is triggered by this business model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, in coordination with the relevant Territorial Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 5 (Administrative Office Use). The activity is a non-industrial, low-environmental-impact professional consultancy operating from a standard commercial office tenancy. It does not fall within Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 or the EPA prescribed list of activities requiring a full Environmental Impact Assessment or a resource consent. No EIA report, no air discharge permit, and no land-use consent is required solely by reason of the business activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to this non-manufacturing service entity. Baseline obligations include: (i) wastewater from sanitary facilities discharged to the municipal sewerage reticulation system under the local Territorial Authority's trade waste and wastewater bylaws; (ii) office refuse and recyclables handled through the council-approved waste collection service under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; (iii) no volatile organic compounds (VOCs), no trade waste, no particulate emissions, and no hazardous waste streams generated by desk-based regulatory consulting. If the company later expands into laboratory testing or device repackaging, a resource consent and EPA assessment would then be reassessed by the applicable district and regional councils.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Building Compliance: The commercial office premises must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) under the Building Act 2004, verified by the Territorial Authority, including scheduled inspections of specified systems (fire alarms, emergency lighting, sprinklers) by an Independent Qualified Person (IQP). Compliance with the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) Act 2017 requires an evacuation procedure and annual fire evacuation training for staff. Occupational Health and Safety: As a Person Conducting a Business or Undertaking (PCBU) under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, the company must implement a written health and safety policy, conduct hazard identification and risk assessments, appoint a competent health and safety officer, provide first-aid equipment and trained first-aiders, and ensure worker engagement and participation. Structural Clearance: The leased premises must comply with the Building (Earthquake-prone Buildings) Amendment Act 2016 structural load and seismic ratings, and any alteration or fit-out must receive a building consent under the Building Act 2004 prior to occupation. In addition, the workplace must comply with the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment workplace amenities codes (ventilation, lighting, sanitary facilities).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand's national tax authority; principal portal is myIR Secure Online Services at https://www.ird.govt.nz, including IRD Gateway API services for tax return and GST filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand limited company, the IRD number is procured automatically upon registration with the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993; the Registrar passes company details to Inland Revenue, which issues the company's tax file number (IRD number). A non-resident company deriving New Zealand-source income or making supplies subject to New Zealand GST must apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number using the appropriate non-resident company application form and must provide certified constitutional documents, director identification, registered office or care-of address details, and ultimate beneficial ownership information. Where a non-resident entity is carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand or supplying remote or digital services to New Zealand consumers, it must also complete GST registration through the Inland Revenue online GST registration portal. There is no standard fee for IRD registration, but all corporate documents in a foreign language must be accompanied by certified English translations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime. Taxation of a limited liability company occurs at the entity level under the Income Tax Act 2007, at the 28% corporate tax rate, with the New Zealand imputation credit system attached to shareholder dividends. Available statutory elections include: GST registration election once taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000; GST accounting basis election between cash and invoice basis; GST taxable period election; tax consolidation election for wholly-owned New Zealand resident company groups under Subpart IG of the Income Tax Act 2007; loss grouping and offset elections; and imputation credit account elections. Hybrid mismatch provisions under the Income Tax Act 2007 apply as mandatory anti-avoidance rules rather than elective entity classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in any 12-month period; applies to resident suppliers and to non-resident suppliers of remote services and low-value imported physical goods under the New Zealand GST remote-services rules. Suppliers below the threshold may choose to register voluntarily but, once registered, must typically remain registered for a minimum of two years.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory government-authorised clearance API applies in New Zealand. Inland Revenue accepts GST returns electronically through myIR and approved Gateway API channels. B2B e-invoicing using the Peppol framework is optional and encouraged for interoperability, but New Zealand does not mandate continuous transaction controls or pre-supply tax authority clearance. Large GST-registered persons with annual turnover exceeding NZD 24 million generally file monthly; smaller taxpayers may qualify for two-month or six-month filing cycles, and all GST payments are settled through electronic banking channels.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A New Zealand GST-registered supplier may zero-rate exports under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when goods are supplied by way of actual physical export from New Zealand and the supplier holds evidence sufficient to satisfy the Inland Revenue Department that export has occurred. Zero-rating also applies to services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied to a New Zealand resident and are not directly connected with land or goods in New Zealand. Services performed on exported movable personal property and certain intellectual property supplies to non-residents may also qualify. The supplier must retain contemporaneous records proving the export, including customs declarations, transport documents, contract terms, insurance, and payment receipts, and must maintain such documentation for at least seven years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service electronic filing via the Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving receipt of foreign currency consideration
Certificate of origin or regulatory export attestation where required
Insurance and freight documentation or transport contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand Customs Service apply rigorous scrutiny to claimed zero-rated export supplies. If goods are not physically exported or services fail the statutory zero-rating conditions, the supplier is liable to reassess GST at 15%, effectively clawing back the zero-rating, and must also pay use-of-money interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Knowingly or dishonestly making a false GST return, or knowingly assisting with an incorrect zero-rating claim, constitutes evasion and attracts civil shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the resulting tax shortfall, with criminal prosecution exposure of fines up to NZD 250,000 for companies and NZD 50,000 for individuals, and imprisonment in serious evasion cases. Auditors may recharacterise the supply as taxable if the exporter cannot produce the required customs and proof-of-export bundle, and any input tax credit previously claimed on the export supply is recoverable from the supplier where the zero-rating is invalidated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), acting in concert with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as joint conduct regulator under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised and unrestricted cross-border capital and current account regime. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is freely convertible with no exchange control legislation, no surrender requirements, and no approval gateways for profit remittance or dividend distributions. Non-resident shareholders may inject equity, receive dividends, and repatriate capital without RBNZ or Overseas Investment Office consent, provided the business does not involve sensitive land, significant business assets above the screening threshold, or fishing/quota interests. For a MedTech regulatory consulting firm (ISIC 7490) with no sensitive-asset exposure, convertibility is effectively unhindered for both capital and current account transactions. The only compliance overlay is the mandatory tax reporting under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Financial Transactions Reporting Act (incorporated within the AML/CFT regime), requiring accurate classification of payment purpose codes for the recipient bank's statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules in New Zealand. A resident exporter of services (including FDA 510(k) and CE Mark compliance consultancy) may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts in an approved New Zealand or offshore bank account, may convert to NZD at any time, and is under no obligation to repatriate. No minimum conversion ratio applies. The only mandatory obligations are (i) accurate recording of the transaction on the exporter's own books, (ii) potential GST zero-rating for exported qualifying services under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, and (iii) statutory record-keeping for income tax purposes and AML/CFT audit trails.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD & USD multi-currency) and segregated Escrow Account for client FDA/CE fee collections
Operational Account with dedicated USD/EUR/GBP sub-accounts for cross-border fee settlement
Primary Corporate Operational Account and foreign currency clearing hub (FX direct dealer)
Operational Account with trade finance line for potential commercial LC issuance to EU/US clients
Secondary Operational Account for domestic NZD disbursements and payroll

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary collections and payments, but NOT a substitute for a licensed New Zealand bank account. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Currenxie, Revolut Business) are permissible as supplementary payment rails, subject to two binding constraints: (i) the EMI must be duly licensed in its home jurisdiction and pass the NZ bank's correspondent due diligence; (ii) where the NZ_LTD maintains its principal operating account at a licensed registered bank (as required by the Companies Act 1993 and the AML/CFT Act), the EMI may only process low-value operational receipts from overseas clients and must not be used for the segregated escrow account that holds client-mandated regulatory filing fees. The Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 requires any person providing financial services to be registered on the FSP Register, but an NZ limited company using an EMI as a pure collection vehicle is not itself deemed a financial service provider. Direct inbound transfers from the EMI to the NZ bank account are treated as ordinary cross-border wires subject to standard purpose-code verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Low_Risk_Standard-grade consulting entity (ISIC 7490), New Zealand banks do not mandate a physical appearance of directors at a branch. Remote onboarding is universally available and typically conducted via video-verified identity (eID) using the NZBN, Companies Office extract, and certified passports. A live video conference with a senior compliance officer is required for the final beneficial ownership confirmation (when any non-resident shareholder holds >25%). Physical presence becomes mandatory only in high-risk scenarios, none of which apply here. However, at least one director must hold a valid passport and present proof of residential address (in their home jurisdiction) to satisfy the Customer Due Diligence / Beneficial Ownership information requirements of the AML/CFT Act 2009. The client risk classification is 'Standard' because the entity is a professional-regulatory consultancy without cash-intensive operations, without high-risk geopolitical exposure, and with no politically exposed persons in the control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) residing outside NZ and absence of a local trust/contact history triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD) review by the bank's Financial Crime Risk team
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of all UBO passports; audited or signed financial statements; a detailed corporate structure chart identifying ultimate natural persons; a signed statutory declaration confirming source of funds and source of wealth; a copy of the shareholders' agreement; and a letter from the company's authorised New Zealand-based tax agent (CAANZ member) confirming tax residency and ongoing compliance obligations

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between bank account stated purpose ('regulatory consulting') and inbound wires from high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., clients based in countries flagged by FATF) triggers the suspicious activity reporting trigger under Section 40 of the AML/CFT Act
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client service agreements with named US/EU medical device manufacturers; FDA 510(k) filing confirmation or CE Mark technical documentation summary; a country-by-country client list with commercial rationale; and a written treasury policy confirming that the account is used exclusively for advisory fees and regulatory filing reimbursements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds (wire in, wire out) without accruing NZD balance, being typical of a pass-through/remittance pattern, triggers an automatic compliance alert under the bank's transaction monitoring rules
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An invoice schedule and payment reconciliation ledger; evidence of professional services rendered (finalised 510(k) or CE submissions); a clear internal treasury policy (dated and board-approved) outlining that outbound payments represent either (a) reimbursement of FDA/CE filing fees to regulatory agencies or (b) subcontractor payments to clinical testing laboratories in the US/EU; plus a notarised manager's certificate confirming no layering of funds

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a private personal account at the same bank for company funds while awaiting company registration completion triggers a red-flag pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Companies Office Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN certificate; director's declaration that all company transactions are recorded in the company's ledger; and a trail of the eventual migration of funds to the corporate account with clear purpose codes

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: Non-resident shareholders remit equity contributions by SWIFT MT103 with the payment narrative of 'Inbound Equity Contribution - NZ_LTD Share Capital'. The purpose code under the RBNZ BOP statistical framework is 'Equity Capital' (Category 6.1 of the RBNZ standard). The bank requires the following verification evidence: (i) a board resolution authorising the share issue; (ii) the shareholder register entry updated under the Companies Act 1993; (iii) proof of source of funds (bank statement from remitting account); and (iv) the NZ Companies Office annual return confirmation of the new shareholding. There is no minimum capital requirement (the Companies Act 1993 imposes no statutory minimum), but for banking onboarding purposes a minimum working-capital injection of NZD 20,000–50,000 is commercially advisable to demonstrate solvency. A foreign direct investment (FDI) report to the Overseas Investment Office is NOT required because the activity is a non-sensitive service business under ISIC 7490, below the significant-business-assets threshold and with no land interest.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For client refunds or vendor/subcontractor payments, the preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 via the NZ bank's high-value electronic clearing system. Domestic NZD payments (e.g., payment of salaries, GST to Inland Revenue, rent) settle through the RBNZ-operated Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), which is a real-time gross settlement (RTGS) infrastructure with intraday finality. Cross-currency disbursements to FDA contractors and EU notified bodies are executed via correspondent banking networks (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR through CHIPS/Fedwire in the US and TARGET2 in the EU). For larger commitments above NZD 50,000, a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit) may be issued by the NZ bank in favour of the EU Notified Body or US testing laboratory, governed by UCP 600, with the required technical documentation (Certificate of Conformity, commercial invoice, and delivery confirmation). The commercial LC route is nevertheless exceptional for consulting engagements; the standard rail remains MT103 wire transfer. Credit card charges are accepted from overseas clients via the bank's acquiring solution with settled funds credited to the NZD operating account within T+2.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain Vanilla FX Forward Contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP) with contract maturities of up to 12 months and no premium; executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's standard FX terms, available without RBNZ authorisation

Foreign Exchange Options (call and put, European-style) on the same deliverable currency pairs, with a capped premium of 2–4% of notional value, used to hedge discrete USD/EUR fee receipts from FDA/CE clients
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for structural hedging of multi-year euro-denominated deferred fee receivables, requiring board approval and a commercial rationale memo

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) restricted to hedging receivables from clients in emerging-market jurisdictions (e.g., CNY, KRW, INR) where the underlying currency is not freely deliverable; contracts must be documented as cash-settled in NZD via the NZ bank's NDF desk and are allowable without official exchange-control approval, though they require a signed suitability letter confirming the underlying trade exposure

Collateralised Overnight Indexed Swaps (OIS) in NZD placed domestically to manage short-term liquidity against floating-rate operating borrowings (only if a working-capital overdraft facility is later established)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Company (online Companies Office annual return) confirming company details, registered office, directors, shareholders, and shareholding structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Te Pōkai Here Kaupapa Roa), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 28 working days after the anniversary of incorporation; the Companies Office issues a pre-due-date reminder notice to the registered office/agent approximately 30 days prior to the AR date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continued non-filing triggers the Registrar's notice of intention to remove the company from the New Zealand register under Companies Act 1993 s318(1)(a); strike-off dissolves the company and vests its assets in the Crown; directors face personal liability for debts incurred during trading after removal, restoration requires a court application or re-registration with additional fees, and directors may be prosecuted for failing to deliver returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (IR4) including corporate financial information and tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date the return is due by 7 July; terminal tax is due 7 April; provisional tax instalments for the following year fall due in August, January, and May for standard balance-date filers if residual income tax exceeds NZD 5,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic tardy filing penalty of NZD 100, escalating to NZD 500 after sustained default; use-of-money interest applies at 9.55% per annum compounded on unpaid and late-reported tax; persistent non-compliance may trigger IRD default assessments, debt collection, and enforcement against company assets, with possible director liability for unpaid employee deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Fringe Benefit Tax Annual Return (IR420) for employer-provided benefits; applicable only if the company provides benefits to employees or shareholder-employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual FBT payers must file by 20 June following the 31 March balance date; quarterly FBT payers file by 20 September, 20 December, 20 March, and 20 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NZD 100 for the first event and NZD 500 for subsequent events; use-of-money interest at 9.55% per annum; failure to file permits IRD default assessments and debt-collection proceedings, and directors can be personally liable if FBT deductions are applied dishonestly.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Auditor's Report delivered to the Registrar; applicable only for 'large' companies, FMC reporting entities, or companies subject to a valid 5% shareholder audit requisition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be completed within 5 months of balance date; copies must be sent to shareholders within 5 months of balance date; audited financial statements required to be filed must be delivered to the Companies Office within 20 working days of being signed and presented
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each director commits an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; the Registrar may impose penalties of up to NZD 50,000 per director and may also obtain compliance orders; failure to present accounts to shareholders renders the annual report ineffective and may trigger shareholder requisition remedies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory for (i) FMC reporting entities (issuers, banks, insurers and similar financial market participants); (ii) non-exempt 'large' for-profit entities under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 with total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees; and (iii) any New Zealand company whose shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares validly requisition an audit within 20 working days of receiving the financial statements. Small companies below all thresholds are exempt from audit unless shareholders serve a requisition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: XRB Accounting Standards Framework: Tier 1 entities apply NZ IFRS in full; Tier 2 large non-publicly-accountable entities apply NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR); Tier 3 eligible for-profit entities apply New Zealand For-profit Simple Format Reporting (Tier 3 NZ SFR); financial statements must be prepared for a 12-month reporting period, commonly aligned to a 31 March balance date, in New Zealand dollars unless directors approve a functional currency presentation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently impose a standalone annual UBO filing obligation; the Annual Return is sworn as a declaration and must accurately state the names and addresses of all current directors and individuals holding shares in the company. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and lodged with the Companies Office by notice within 10 working days of registration. The Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Bill, once in force, will require a beneficial ownership statement to accompany the Annual Return; pending that legislation, AML/CFT Act 2009 obligations require regulated reporting entities to verify and retain beneficial ownership information on a continuous risk-based customer due diligence basis.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholder resolutions and board minutes)
Interests Register (directors' interests under Companies Act 1993 s140)
Registered office records: certificate of incorporation, constitution (if any), and share transfer instruments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,400 per annum (registered-office-only services approximately USD 200–400; full registered agent and company secretarial compliance retainer approximately USD 450–1,400; nominee officer services for non-resident directors billed separately)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–12,000 per annum for a compulsory statutory audit of a small-to-mid-sized New Zealand Ltd; an independent review engagement is typically USD 2,000–5,000; not budgeted unless shareholder requisition, large-company threshold, or lender/investor covenant triggers the requirement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays or preferential corporate income tax rate exist in New Zealand. Available reliefs for qualifying MedTech regulatory consulting activities include: (i) a 15% R&D tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure; (ii) a refundable 28% R&D loss tax credit for qualifying loss-making companies performing eligible R&D; (iii) ordinary depreciation deductions and immediate deductions for certain low-value plant and equipment; and (iv) standard grouping and loss offset rules. Consulting fees from FDA 510(k) and European CE Mark compliance work are ordinary assessable income and are not eligible for an industry-specific exemption.
